newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish FinMin sets EBR at 637mln punts, 1.6 pct GNP.
newsitem.headline: Irish FinMin sets EBR at 637mln punts, 1.6 pct GNP.

text.p: Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn targetted a 1997 Exchequer Borrowing Requirement (EBR) of 637 million punts, 1.6 percent of Gross National Product (GNP), in his budget speech on Wednesday.
Economists' forecasts for the post-budget EBR ranged from 585 million punts to 755 million. A pre-budget White Paper showed the opening EBR position at 380 million punts.
The EBR for 1996 was 437 million punts or 1.2 percent of GNP, compared with an official budget day target for 1996 of 729 million or 2.0 percent of GNP.
The 1996 current budget was in surplus to the tune of 292 million as against an expected deficit of 82 million punts.
Quinn said he had made provisions for a current budget surplus of 193 million pounds in 1997, equivalent to 0.5 percent of GNP.
He also pencilled in a General Government Deficit of 1.5 percent of GDP, well below the three percent limit set by the Maastricht Treaty.

"This is the first time ever that a Minister of Finance has planned for a significant current budget surplus," Quinn said in his budget speech to parliament. "And I am projecting a surplus not just for one year, 1997, but for 1998 and 1999 as well."
Quinn said taking account of departmental balances of 26 million pounds and increased capital receipts of 20 million pounds, the opening EBR for 1997 is 334 million Irish pounds.
